summary: Verified the Windows installer bugfix (setup_windows.ps1 step 3/7 MongoDB winget fallback). PowerShell syntax validated with a real PowerShell 7.4.6 parser (0 parse errors). CRITICAL FINDING: the hardcoded fallback download URL https://fastdl.mongodb.org/windows/mongodb-windows-x86_64-latest.msi does NOT exist - it returns HTTP 403 AccessDenied (S3 XML error, 243 bytes), so the new fallback will always fail for the user. Versioned URLs from https://downloads.mongodb.org/current.json (e.g. mongodb-windows-x86_64-8.0.29-signed.msi / 8.2.12 / 8.3.8) return HTTP 206 with content-type application/x-msi and are valid. Backend regression: 37/37 pytest tests pass (backend_test.py + test_security_iter2.py), cleanup_iter2.py run afterwards (login_attempts cleared, remaining 0); bcrypt hashes verified $2b$ len=60 for admin/agen/pelanggan; httpOnly cookie set on login; no application code touched by the installer fix.

critical.issue: URL https://fastdl.mongodb.org/windows/mongodb-windows-x86_64-latest.msi returns HTTP 403 AccessDenied (verified via HEAD and ranged GET; body is an S3 AccessDenied XML of 243 bytes). MongoDB does NOT publish a 'latest' MSI alias. Invoke-WebRequest will throw -> script hits Fail() -> the whole winget-0x8a15000f fix does not actually work. Must use a versioned URL, preferably resolved dynamically: Invoke-RestMethod https://downloads.mongodb.org/current.json, pick versions[] where production_release=true and downloads[] target='windows', edition='base' -> .msi, with a hardcoded verified fallback such as https://fastdl.mongodb.org/windows/mongodb-windows-x86_64-8.0.29-signed.msi (verified 206, application/x-msi).

No administrator-elevation check. msiexec ADDLOCAL=ServerService (installs a Windows service) and Start-Service MongoDB both require elevation; without it msiexec returns exit 1603/1625 and the user gets a confusing failure. Add a self-elevation block at the top (WindowsPrincipal IsInRole Administrator -> Start-Process powershell -Verb RunAs) or hard-fail with a clear message.

Installer writes CORS_ORIGINS="http://localhost:3000" but writes frontend/.env with REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=http://<LAN-IP>:8001 and tells the user (line 123) to open http://<LAN-IP>:3000. Browser origin http://<LAN-IP>:3000 is not in allow_origins (server.py builds allow_origins strictly from CORS_ORIGINS), so every API call from the LAN IP / from a phone is blocked by CORS. Generate CORS_ORIGINS="http://localhost:3000,http://<ip>:3000".

minor.issue: Start-Service MongoDB uses -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue and then Ok "MongoDB berjalan" is printed unconditionally - a false success if the service fails to start. Re-query Get-Service and Fail if Status -ne 'Running'.

Invoke-WebRequest on Windows PowerShell 5.1 renders a progress bar for a ~350 MB download making it extremely slow/appear hung. Set $ProgressPreference='SilentlyContinue' (and [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12 for older Win10 builds) before the download.

No sanity check on the downloaded file before running msiexec (e.g. (Get-Item $msi).Length -gt 50MB). A small HTML/XML error page written to disk would be handed to msiexec producing a cryptic 1620 error.
winget stdout/stderr fully suppressed (2>$null | Out-Null), so users/support get no diagnostics for the original 0x8a15000f error. Capture output to a log file under $env:TEMP.

Informational: cookie uses secure=True + samesite=none, which browsers reject over plain http:// on the LAN deployment this installer creates. App still works because frontend/src/lib/api.js falls back to a Bearer token from localStorage; keep that fallback.

action_items: Replace the dead 'latest' MSI URL in setup_windows.ps1 with a version resolved from https://downloads.mongodb.org/current.json plus a verified hardcoded fallback (8.0.29-signed.msi) - the current fallback ALWAYS fails (403).
Add administrator elevation check / self-elevation before msiexec service install and Start-Service.
Generate CORS_ORIGINS including the detected LAN IP origin (http://<ip>:3000) in backend/.env.
Verify service status after Start-Service instead of printing unconditional 'MongoDB berjalan'.
Add $ProgressPreference='SilentlyContinue', TLS 1.2 enforcement, and a downloaded-file size check around the MSI download.
critical_code_review_comments: Never hardcode a vendor 'latest' artifact path without verifying it exists; MongoDB only publishes versioned signed MSIs (current.json is the supported discovery endpoint).

PowerShell parse validated with PowerShell 7.4.6 Parser::ParseFile => 0 errors; here-string @"..."@ closed correctly, braces balanced, Step/Ok/Fail defined before first use, only Windows-only cmdlets (Get-Service, Start-Service, Get-NetIPAddress, winget) unresolvable on Linux as expected.
Fallback control flow itself is sound (winget attempt -> $wingetOk service probe -> download -> msiexec -> re-probe Get-Service -> Fail or continue); no dangling path, no unreachable branch.
seed_data_creation: None persisted. Test suite created transient QA users; /app/backend/tests/cleanup_iter2.py executed afterwards (4 synthetic QA users deleted, 3 login_attempts cleared, 0 remaining) so demo accounts are not locked.

context_for_next_testing_agent: PowerShell 7.4.6 (arm64) is installed at /opt/pwsha/pwsh and a parser-check script exists at /tmp/parse_check.ps1 (copy to /app if it must persist) - use it to statically validate setup_windows.ps1. Verify any new MongoDB download URL with: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' -r 0-2047 <url> (expect 206 application/x-msi; 403 means the key does not exist). Always run 'python tests/cleanup_iter2.py' from /app/backend after the pytest suite.
rca_of_the_issue: The developer added a MongoDB MSI fallback using the guessed URL '.../mongodb-windows-x86_64-latest.msi'. That S3 object does not exist, so CloudFront/S3 returns 403 AccessDenied; Invoke-WebRequest raises a terminating error, the catch block calls Fail() and the installer stops - identical user-visible outcome to the original winget 0x8a15000f failure. Mitigation: resolve the current production Windows base MSI from https://downloads.mongodb.org/current.json (verified working, e.g. 8.0.29/8.2.12/8.3.8 signed MSIs return 206 application/x-msi) with a hardcoded versioned fallback.
